restrictions.location: Ookwemin St 7 m Southeast of Villiers St to 93 m Southeast of Villiers St
restrictions.reason: Toronto-TMC: The proposed scope of work includes the advancement of 5 boreholes to a maximum depth of fifteen (15) metres below grade (mbg) within the roadway and public right-of-way along northwest portion of Ookwemin Street. All 5 boreholes will be completed as monitoring wells using 50 mm diameter Schedule 40 PVC pipe with 3-metre screens and flushto-grade casings. The work will be conducted using hydrovac to daylight locations first, followed by hollow-stem auguring, and each borehole/monitoring well will be sampled for soil and groundwater. Traffic control measures, including signage, barriers, and personnel, will be implemented where required, and the boreholes may require daylighting to safely expose underground utilities prior to drilling.

restrictions.location: Kipling Ave 11 m South of Bloor St W to 77 m South of Bloor St W
restrictions.reason: Toronto-TMC: The construction of the New Etobicoke Civic Centre. Multiplex Construction Canada will be managing the construction of the New Etobicoke Civic Centre Located at 3755 Bloor Street W. Etobicoke, Ontario M9A 1A2, located within the newly redeveloped Etobicoke Civic Centre Precinct (formerly the Westwood Theatre Lands). The ECC is a mixed-use building comprising a wide range of community focused program and services. The building is arranged in a series of tall volumes towards the north, housing the municipal offices, while the lower floors towards the south contain all the public functions. It will also be compliant to the Toronto Accessibility Design Guidelines (TADG) to extend greater accessibility for all users. With 508,000 square feet of accessible public-facing space, the new civic centre is the first of its kind to be built in the last 50 years and is designed as a state-of-the-art mixed-used civic hub that includes: Civic Square • Approximately 47,000 sq

restrictions.location: Edward St at University Ave to 23 m East of University Ave
restrictions.reason: Toronto-TMC: The United Building is North America’s tallest heritage retention development. A residential tower will rise from the historic Maclean Publishing Company/Maclean-Hunter building in Toronto. The resulting mixed-use 54-storey high-rise will feature the restored heritage structure with offices and retail at the base, and new residences above. This development will offer a rare opportunity to live, work and play on University Avenue, one of Toronto’s most prestigious thoroughfares.

restrictions.location: Sunlight Park Rd at end of road to 33 m West of Broadview Ave
restrictions.reason: Toronto-TMC: The Broadview and Eastern Flood Protection (BEFP) project will address flood vulnerability for urban land east of the Don River, between Eastern Avenue and rail corridor, the existing underpass at Eastern Avenue, and the proposed underpass at Broadview Avenue. As part of this construction, there will be utility relocations and reconstruction in this area, including city storm and sanitary sewers that run along Sunlight Park Rd. Buildings related to one business within the project footprint will be removed to allow for construction of the FPL and other necessary local infrastructure. The removal also enables future projects by others such as the Broadview Avenue Extension, East Harbour Transit Hub & Development and the Ontario Line.
